neighbours.label: the outcome adverb after 'do/did/done' judging how something turned out (did well, do well to, did badly)
fire: The new restaurant did well in its first year despite the recession.
Investors would do well to read the fine print before signing.
Tomatoes do well in sunny spots with plenty of water.
After months of training, she did well at the regional finals.
The film has done well overseas, especially in Korea.
Honestly, our team did poorly in the second half.
Students who skip the labs usually do badly on the final exam.
He thinks the startup will do well once the app launches.
quiet: The new restaurant is well known for its fresh pasta and wine.
Investors were well aware of the risks before signing.
Tomatoes grow in sunny spots with plenty of water.
After months of training, she sang beautifully at the regional finals.
The film is well made, with a strong cast and score.
The old well in the village square dried up last summer.
Students who skip the labs usually understand the material less well.
He thinks the startup will launch the app in the spring.

predictions: 'well', 'badly' or 'poorly' right after do/did/does/done fire; 'well' as a manner adverb after other verbs or as a noun stays quiet.
notes: Probe: 'did well' 0.930, 'do well to add' 0.969, 'did well and sold' 0.747, 'leftovers do well' 0.972, 'party did well' 0.811, 'did badly' 0.718; 'speaks French very well' 0.010, noun 'dug a well' 0.005. So it reads the do-construction's outcome slot, not the word 'well'.
